title: Welsh Rarebit
subtitle: Rich cheddar sauce on toast
excerpt: Welsh rarebit is a cheddar sauce made with milk, butter, flour, and Worcestershire sauce, poured over thick toast and grilled until bubbling and golden. It sounds simple and it is, but the result is one of the most satisfying things you can make in under 15 minutes. Half a teaspoon of mustard powder or prepared English mustard stirred into the sauce adds a pleasant sharpness.
sourceNotes: Welsh rarebit has been documented in British cookbooks since at least the 18th century, originally called Welsh rabbit, a humorous reference to the idea that cheese was the Welshman's substitute for meat. The dish has no rabbit in it; the name is a joke that stuck.

content.text: Use a well-aged cheddar with a sharp flavour. Mild cheddar melts cleanly but lacks the intensity that makes rarebit worth eating.
Melt the butter in the saucepan over medium heat. Add the flour and stir constantly for 1 minute to cook out the raw flour taste.
Gradually pour in the milk, stirring continuously, until the sauce is smooth and beginning to thicken, about 2 minutes.

Remove the pan from the heat. Add the grated cheddar a handful at a time, stirring between each addition until fully melted. Stir in the Worcestershire sauce. If you have mustard powder or prepared English mustard to hand, half a teaspoon stirred in here adds a pleasant sharpness.
Leave the sauce to cool for 1 minute, then stir in the egg yolks one at a time. The residual heat is enough to incorporate them without scrambling.

Toast 4 thick slices of bread. Spread the rarebit sauce generously over each slice. Place under a hot grill for 2 to 3 minutes until the top is bubbling and spotted with golden-brown patches. Serve immediately.

items.cause: The cheese was added when the sauce was too hot, causing the proteins to seize
items.fix: Remove from the heat before adding the cheese. A gentle residual heat melts it smoothly.

items.symptom: The rarebit is running off the toast
items.fix: Let the sauce cool for a couple of minutes before spreading. It will thicken as it cools.
